The pt is a ___ y/o RHM with a history of insulin dependent 
diabetes, hypertension, gout, BPH and CAD s/p stents and CABG 
presented to our ED after waking up with left sided weakness 
since 8 am today.

He states he was in his normal health, getting 
around with no problems until this morning.

Yesterday he was 
pushing his son ___ in the wheelchair with no problems. ___ 
normally gets around by electric wheelchair but it has recently 
broke.

He noted no problems, then today around ___ am as he 
estimates he noted that he awoke to go use the rest room and 
noted that he was falling over to the left.

He noted no light 
headed feeling or vertigo type feeling but did not that his left 
side was weak, both the arm and the leg.

He thought the symptoms 
would resolve and that this would end up being a TIA as he is a 
retired doctor (___) but this was not the case.

Since 
his weakness had not resolved, but also had not gotten worse he 
decided to come to the ED for further care.

questioning he notes that his speech is a little slurred,
___ is his second language as he is originally from ___

___ is an ___ year old right handed man with history 
significant for HTN, insulin dependent DM and CAD who comes in 
for evaluation of left sided weakness and dysarthria and was 
found to have a new pontine infarct on MRI.

MRI also shows some 
chronic infarcts that may also be contributing to his complaints 
and deficits on physical exam.

Patient has risk profile 
worrisome for stroke and appears to have old strokes on imaging.

No history of atrial fibrillation and this doesn't seem c/w with 
an embolic stroke but need to rule out embolic etiologies to be 
sure.

While in house his home lisinopril was 
held and his blood pressure was allowed to autoregulate.
Neuro checks were done q4 hours.

His weakness may 
have progressed a very small bit while in house but this is hard 
to tell.

He was seen with physical therapy and occupational 
therapy ___ and we agreed.

He was continued on his home Aspirin 
and Plavix and told to continue taking these medications.

has stable angina and is not currently having CP/SOB.
